sec: Amiodarone thyroid disease and drug-induced thyroiditis

items.q: Match the following amiodarone thyroid pattern — 1) Type 1 2) Type 2 3) Euthyroid 4) Subclinical hypothyroidism on amiodarone … A) Iodine-induced hyperthyroidism B) Destructive thyroiditis C) Hormone release with normal TFTs D) Mildly raised TSH, normal free T4
items.exp: Type 1 is iodine-induced hyperthyroidism in predisposed glands; Type 2 is destructive thyroiditis with low uptake; many patients remain euthyroid; subclinical hypothyroidism can occur especially in iodine-replete regions. (Book p916)

items.q: A cardiac patient on amiodarone develops weight loss with suppressed TSH and very low uptake on scan. The most consistent diagnosis is:
items.exp: Low uptake on scan in an amiodarone-treated patient fits destructive (Type 2) thyrotoxicosis; Type 1 has preserved or increased uptake. (Book p916)

items.q: Assess amiodarone thyroid disease: I Type 1 occurs in abnormal glands (nodules or latent Graves). II Type 2 occurs in normal glands via destructive thyroiditis.
items.exp: Type 1 typically requires underlying nodular or autoimmune disease; Type 2 occurs even in normal glands because of direct toxicity and release of preformed hormone. (Book p916)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a treatment for Type 2 amiodarone thyrotoxicosis?
opts: Thyroidectomy if severe and amiodarone cannot be stopped
items.exp: Type 2 responds to corticosteroids; thionamides are largely ineffective in destructive thyroiditis, making them the odd one out for first-line use. (Book p916)

items.q: The half-life of amiodarone and its iodine load means amiodarone thyroid disease can develop up to ___ after stopping therapy.
items.exp: Amiodarone's long half-life (50–100 days) and iodine load mean thyroid disease can occur or persist for many months after discontinuation. (Book p916)

items.q: Match the following drug to its thyroid effect — 1) Lithium 2) Interferon-α 3) Immune checkpoint inhibitors 4) Amiodarone … A) Inhibits hormone release B) Often reversible thyroiditis C) Can cause thyroiditis / hypo- or hyperthyroidism D) Both hypothyroidism and thyrotoxicosis via iodine load
items.exp: Lithium inhibits hormone release; IFN-α commonly causes reversible thyroiditis; ICIs can cause thyroiditis with hypo- or hyperthyroidism; amiodarone causes both via its iodine load. (Book p916)

items.q: A patient on pembrolizumab develops new atrial fibrillation with suppressed TSH and a low uptake scan. The next best diagnostic step is:
opts: Diagnose ICI-induced thyroiditis and treat with beta-blocker ± steroids
items.exp: ICI-induced thyroiditis typically presents as thyrotoxicosis with low uptake; treat with beta-blocker and steroids if severe. (Book p916)

items.q: Assess ICI thyroid toxicity: I Hypothyroidism often follows the thyrotoxic phase. II ICIs never cause Graves-like disease.
items.exp: ICI-induced biphasic thyroiditis is common, with hypothyroid phase following the thyrotoxic phase; rare Graves-like disease is reported but unusual. (Book p916)

items.q: Match the following diagnostic clue — 1) IL-6 elevation 2) High uptake with vascular nodule 3) Preserved uptake in iodine-replete gland 4) Anti-TPO and anti-Tg antibodies … A) Type 2 amiodarone thyrotoxicosis B) Type 1 amiodarone thyrotoxicosis C) Autoimmune predisposition D) Hashimoto thyroiditis
items.exp: IL-6 rise supports Type 2 destructive thyroiditis; high uptake with a vascular nodule fits Type 1; preserved uptake in iodine-replete gland suggests an autoimmune predisposition; anti-TPO/Tg point to Hashimoto. (Book p916)

items.q: A 65-year-old on amiodarone for AF develops overt hypothyroidism; the cardiac team is unwilling to stop amiodarone. The most consistent therapy is:
items.exp: Amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism is treated with levothyroxine; amiodarone is continued if needed for cardiac control. (Book p916)

items.q: Amiodarone contains approximately ___ mg of iodine per 200 mg tablet (each tablet carries a large iodine load).
items.exp: Each 200 mg tablet of amiodarone contains about 75 mg of iodine; this massive iodine load is the basis of its thyroid effects. (Book p916)

items.q: Assess amiodarone's iodine: I Daily iodine release greatly exceeds the WHO recommended intake. II Iodine excess can transiently inhibit organification (Wolff-Chaikoff effect).
items.exp: Amiodarone releases ~7 mg of iodine daily, far above WHO recommendations; Wolff-Chaikoff effect describes transient inhibition of organification by iodine excess. (Book p916)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among drugs listed as causing thyroiditis?
items.exp: Levothyroxine is replacement therapy, not a cause of thyroiditis; IFN-α, ICIs and amiodarone are recognised triggers. (Book p916)
